thread.title: How AMD's Revenue Drivers Are Alive And Well - Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD)

author: Chris Lau
title: How AMD's Revenue Drivers Are Alive And Well - Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD)
text:
As CES 2019 gets underway from Jan. 8-11, savvy technology investors will question if the seasonal strength pushing shares of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) back to $20 will last. Two other factors also will drive AMD’s stock price in the coming weeks and months. Near term, the quarterly earnings call sometime later this month will undo the last sell-off. And a refresh in Ryzen chips may finally give investors confidence in AMD accelerating market share gains against its rival Intel ( INTC ).
AMD rose ~ 9% in the last week ahead of CES 2019, plus a general rebound in stocks renewed buying interest. CES usually marks a seasonal end for technology stocks. As markets price in the announcements ahead of the show, tech firms do not have any new catalysts. Still, strong quarterly earnings from companies in this sector may counter the seasonal selling. This year, there are two notable exceptions whose weakness may spread to AMD stock. IBM ( IBM ) is likely to report another weak quarter and may lower its outlook, citing slower customer spending and a slowdown caused by the U.S.-China trade negotiations now underway.
Apple ( AAPL ), whose quarterly earnings warning shook up markets and sent its stock to yearly lows, will face at least one or two more quarters of weakness. The best-case scenario is that the U.S. and China settle on a fair deal that does not lead to weakened demand for Apple devices.
Investors will logically ask why Apple’s weakness would hurt AMD stock, especially when iPhone demand hurts PC and notebook sales. Markets treat Apple as a safe play, so if its 10.8 times forward P/E still leads to the stock’s decline, then AMD at 30.6 times forward P/E looks even less appealing. In the short term, Apple and AMD stock will have a high correlation to each other. It is only if or when AMD’s quarterly report signals strength in all segments – from CPU to GPU – that the two stocks will trade independently of each other.
Q4 Earnings Estimates
Source: Tipranks
The consensus estimate for AMD’s Q4/2018 earnings is $0.06 a share, unchanged from last year’s results. That AMD succeeded to rally back from the ~$17 low in recent months suggests that the market is not looking for a sharp turnaround in earnings. It does expect revenue growth in all of AMD’s segments. Analysts also are looking for data points that signal market share growth in the PC and notebook market.
On the GPU side, investors should expect another low, disappointing quarter. The industry is still working through a supply glut for graphics cards. Nvidia ( NVDA ) said last quarter that it has 8 – 12 weeks of inventory to work through. Its latest RTX card announcement, priced at $350, now gives consumers a more affordable solution for ray tracing. At this price, the card competes with AMD’s Vega card, even though Vega supply is limited due to manufacturing constraints for HBM2 memory.
Ryzen Progress Leaks of Ryzen 7 3700X and Ryzen 5 3600X, which are AMD’s first Zen 2 based 7nm desktop, are nothing short of impressive. Having more cores and more speed (5 GHz), the competitive pricing will give Intel a run for the money.

Ryzen 5 3600G: $199
Ryzen 5 3600: $178
Ryzen 3 3300X: $129
Ryzen 3 3300G: $129
Ryzen 3 3300: $99
Source: TechRadar
Note that Intel still has a command in the PC market due to its marketing budget and the preference for suppliers to sell Intel. But at the prices noted above, AMD has an integrated chipset solution (3300G, 3600G), more powerful built-in graphics, and a better price than Intel’s Celeron, Pentium or i3 solutions.
Price Target and Your Takeaway I'm not ready to re-establish a downside entry price or target price for AMD stock, although it's brought up in live chat on the DIY Value Investing marketplace . In one article posted last year, AMD traded within the AMD price target of $30 - $35, only to pull back to the $27 range and then ultimately fall following its earnings. Wait for AMD to first report EPYC sales exceeding expectations and healthy Ryzen sales for PC and notebooks.
